turns.content: Hi, I'm working on an article about child and maternal health in South Asia and could use some reliable data to start with. Could you help me find clear statistics with proper sources?

**Intent:** You’re writing an article on child and maternal health in South Asia and need clear, citable statistics with solid sources.

Below is a compact set of headline indicators for **Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka** using the **latest available data** from World Bank databases (mainly WDI/HNP).

---

## Data

### 1. Under‑5 mortality rate (per 1,000 live births, latest year)

| Country        | Year | Under‑5 mortality (per 1,000 live births) |
|---------------|------|--------------------------------------------|
| Afghanistan   | 2023 | <claim id="21d88631" policy="auto">55.5</claim> |
| Pakistan      | 2023 | <claim id="36f3baa7" policy="auto">58.5</claim> |
| India         | 2023 | <claim id="b0c8528d" policy="auto">27.7</claim> |
| Bangladesh    | 2023 | <claim id="255dc075" policy="auto">30.6</claim> |
| Nepal         | 2023 | <claim id="3a010449" policy="auto">26.5</claim> |
| Bhutan        | 2023 | <claim id="046ed96f" policy="auto">23.1</claim> |
| Sri Lanka     | 2023 | <claim id="a620014b" policy="auto">6.1</claim> |
| Maldives      | 2023 | <claim id="4906d30c" policy="auto">5.7</claim> |

**Source indicator:** *Mortality rate, under‑5 (per 1,000 live births)* — **World Bank WDI**, code **SH.DYN.MORT** (Data360: `WB_WDI_SH_DYN_MORT`)

---

### 2. Maternal mortality ratio (per 100,000 live births, latest year)

| Country        | Year | Maternal mortality ratio (per 100,000 live births) |
|---------------|------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| Afghanistan   | 2023 | <claim id="24134a8b" policy="auto">521</claim> |
| Pakistan      | 2023 | <claim id="7cb077bf" policy="auto">155</claim> |
| Nepal         | 2023 | <claim id="4f348921" policy="auto">142</claim> |
| Bangladesh    | 2023 | <claim id="58c9147c" policy="auto">115</claim> |
| India         | 2023 | <claim id="bfb17fa3" policy="auto">80</claim> |
| Bhutan        | 2023 | <claim id="b6bdaf32" policy="auto">47</claim> |
| Maldives      | 2023 | <claim id="c25d428a" policy="auto">32</claim> |
| Sri Lanka     | 2023 | <claim id="bf8e9daa" policy="auto">18</claim> |

**Source indicator:** *Maternal mortality ratio (modeled estimate, per 100,000 live births)* — **World Bank WDI**, code **SH.STA.MMRT** (Data360: `WB_WDI_SH_STA_MMRT`)

---

### 3. Births attended by skilled health staff (% of total)

Latest observations are somewhat patchy; this is what’s available in 2018–2021:

| Country    | Year (latest) | Births attended by skilled staff (% of total) |
|-----------|----------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Afghanistan | 2020 | <claim id="d164e509" policy="auto">61.8</claim>% |
| Bangladesh  | 2019 | <claim id="61c90145" policy="auto">59</claim>% |
| Bhutan      | 2021 | <claim id="e153f521" policy="auto">98.9</claim>% |
| India       | 2021 | <claim id="487a0669" policy="auto">89.4</claim>% |
| Nepal       | 2019 | <claim id="22b55eaa" policy="auto">77.2</claim>% |
| Pakistan    | 2020 | <claim id="2cad60e0" policy="auto">68</claim>% |

(Maldives and Sri Lanka show no recent values in this World Bank series; they are typically very high based on DHS/MICS, but those are not in this extract.)

**Source indicator:** *Births attended by skilled health staff (% of total)* — **World Bank HNP**, code **SH.STA.BRTC.ZS** (Data360: `WB_HNP_SH_STA_BRTC_ZS`)

---

### 4. Child undernutrition – stunting (% of children under 5)

| Country      | Year (latest) | Stunting prevalence (% of under‑5s) |
|-------------|----------------|-------------------------------------|
| Afghanistan | 2022 | <claim id="403c5eb6" policy="auto">44.6</claim>% |
| Pakistan    | 2018 | <claim id="2e155f41" policy="auto">37.6</claim>% |
| India       | 2020 | <claim id="e078ec05" policy="auto">35.5</claim>% |
| Nepal       | 2022 | <claim id="c438f900" policy="auto">24.8</claim>% |
| Bangladesh  | 2022 | <claim id="2b5f89d0" policy="auto">23.6</claim>% |

**Source indicator:** *Prevalence of stunting, height for age (% of children under 5)* — **World Bank HNP**, code **SH.STA.STNT.ZS** (Data360: `WB_HNP_SH_STA_STNT_ZS`)

---

### 5. Child undernutrition – wasting (% of children under 5)

Data are sparser and not synchronized in time across countries; latest available for each:

| Country      | Year (latest) | Wasting prevalence (% of under‑5s) |
|-------------|----------------|------------------------------------|
| India       | 2020 | <claim id="d53fad8c" policy="auto">18.7</claim>% |
| Bangladesh  | 2022 | <claim id="6c24cf1c" policy="auto">11</claim>% |
| Nepal       | 2022 | <claim id="9456eff2" policy="auto">7</claim>% |
| Pakistan    | 2018 | <claim id="17e14151" policy="auto">7.1</claim>% |
| Afghanistan | 2022 | <claim id="c9fe7442" policy="auto">3.6</claim>% |

**Source indicator:** *Prevalence of wasting, weight for height (% of children under 5)* — **World Bank HNP**, code **SH.STA.WAST.ZS** (Data360: `WB_HNP_SH_STA_WAST_ZS`)

---

## Analysis (for narrative use)

- **Huge sub‑regional contrasts:** In 2023, a child in Afghanistan faces an under‑5 mortality rate of <claim id="21d88631" policy="auto">55.5</claim> deaths per 1,000 live births, versus just <claim id="a620014b" policy="auto">6.1</claim> in Sri Lanka and <claim id="4906d30c" policy="auto">5.7</claim> in Maldives. That’s roughly a **9–10‑fold gap** across South Asia.

- **Maternal deaths remain very high in fragile settings:** Afghanistan’s maternal mortality ratio is estimated at <claim id="24134a8b" policy="auto">521</claim> deaths per 100,000 live births (2023), compared with <claim id="bf8e9daa" policy="auto">18</claim> in Sri Lanka and <claim id="c25d428a" policy="auto">32</claim> in Maldives — closer to high‑income levels.

- **Coverage of skilled birth attendance is rising but uneven:** India has nearly **universal coverage**, with about <claim id="487a0669" policy="auto">89.4</claim>% of births attended by skilled health staff (2021), and Bhutan is almost at <claim id="e153f521" policy="auto">98.9</claim>% (2021). Pakistan lags at around <claim id="2cad60e0" policy="auto">68</claim>% (2020), and Bangladesh at <claim id="61c90145" policy="auto">59</claim>% (2019).

- **Chronic undernutrition is still pervasive:** Around **one‑third** of young children are stunted in several countries: India (<claim id="e078ec05" policy="auto">35.5</claim>%, 2020), Pakistan (<claim id="2e155f41" policy="auto">37.6</claim>%, 2018), Afghanistan (<claim id="403c5eb6" policy="auto">44.6</claim>%, 2022). Bangladesh and Nepal have improved but still have roughly **one in four** under‑5s stunted (<claim id="2b5f89d0" policy="auto">23.6</claim>% and <claim id="c438f900" policy="auto">24.8</claim>%, respectively, 2022).

- **Acute undernutrition (wasting) is particularly severe in India:** India’s wasting prevalence of <claim id="d53fad8c" policy="auto">18.7</claim>% (2020) is among the highest in the world and far above Bangladesh (<claim id="6c24cf1c" policy="auto">11</claim>%, 2022), Nepal (<claim id="9456eff2" policy="auto">7</claim>%, 2022), and Pakistan (<claim id="17e14151" policy="auto">7.1</claim>%, 2018).

---

## Limitations / Caveats

- **Different reference years:** Nutrition and skilled birth attendance data are from different years by country (2018–2022). For precise comparisons, note the year in your text.
- **Modeled estimates:** Maternal mortality figures are **modeled** WHO/UN inter‑agency estimates as compiled by the World Bank; they come with uncertainty intervals (not shown here).
- **Missing values:** Some recent values for skilled birth attendance, wasting, and stunting are missing for certain countries; national surveys (DHS, MICS, national health surveys) can complement these.

---

## Sources

- **World Bank — World Development Indicators (WDI)**  
  - *Mortality rate, under‑5 (per 1,000 live births)* — indicator **SH.DYN.MORT** (Data360: `WB_WDI_SH_DYN_MORT`)  
  - *Maternal mortality ratio (modeled estimate, per 100,000 live births)* — indicator **SH.STA.MMRT** (Data360: `WB_WDI_SH_STA_MMRT`)

- **World Bank — Health, Nutrition and Population Statistics (HNP)**  
  - *Births attended by skilled health staff (% of total)* — indicator **SH.STA.BRTC.ZS** (Data360: `WB_HNP_SH_STA_BRTC_ZS`)  
  - *Prevalence of stunting, height for age (% of children under 5)* — indicator **SH.STA.STNT.ZS** (Data360: `WB_HNP_SH_STA_STNT_ZS`)  
  - *Prevalence of wasting, weight for height (% of children under 5)* — indicator **SH.STA.WAST.ZS** (Data360: `WB_HNP_SH_STA_WAST_ZS`)

These are all standard, citable indicators widely used in global health reporting.

---

**Suggested follow‑ups:**

1. “Can you give me a short, publication‑ready paragraph comparing India and Pakistan on these indicators?”  
2. “Could you add trends since 2000 for under‑5 and maternal mortality in South Asia as a whole?”  
3. “Can you help me pull similar indicators for a specific South Asian country I want to profile in depth?”

turns.content: Could you create a clear line chart showing the trends in under-5 mortality and maternal mortality in South Asia from 2000 to 2023?

Here are two ready‑to‑use line charts for your article, covering **2000–2023** for all South Asian countries:

**Data:**

1. **Under‑5 mortality rate (per 1,000 live births), 2000–2023**  
   - Chart URL:  
     [Under‑5 mortality trends in South Asia (2000–2023)](http://localhost:8000/static/viz_specs/13ebad9f-063d-4cae-bb63-66bd266d388a_vega.json)  
   - Countries included: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka  
   - Indicator: *Mortality rate, under‑5 (per 1,000 live births)* — **World Bank WDI**, code **SH.DYN.MORT** (Data360: `WB_WDI_SH_DYN_MORT`)

2. **Maternal mortality ratio (per 100,000 live births), 2000–2023**  
   - Chart URL:  
     [Maternal mortality trends in South Asia (2000–2023)](http://localhost:8000/static/viz_specs/efac254d-117f-473a-b50d-ebaa9ddedb49_vega.json)  
   - Countries included: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka  
   - Indicator: *Maternal mortality ratio (modeled estimate, per 100,000 live births)* — **World Bank WDI**, code **SH.STA.MMRT** (Data360: `WB_WDI_SH_STA_MMRT`)

You can embed these charts (or export images) from the URLs, or load the Vega‑Lite specs into any compatible visualization tool.

**Analysis (how to read them briefly):**

- Both charts show a **steady decline** in under‑5 and maternal mortality across South Asia since 2000, with **Afghanistan and Pakistan** consistently at the high‑mortality end and **Sri Lanka and Maldives** at the low‑mortality end.
- The slopes flatten in some countries after around **2015**, which you can use to discuss slowing progress toward SDG targets.

**Sources:**

- **World Bank — World Development Indicators (WDI)**  
  - SH.DYN.MORT — Mortality rate, under‑5 (per 1,000 live births)  
  - SH.STA.MMRT — Maternal mortality ratio (modeled estimate, per 100,000 live births)

---

2. Can you provide a short narrative caption (2–3 sentences) I can place under each chart?  
3. Could you pull the same trends but aggregated for “South Asia” as a region instead of by country?

**Summary:** I can’t directly build a *single* multi‑indicator Vega spec via the current tools, but you can still get a clean two‑panel figure quite easily by combining the two existing charts.

---

**Data:**

You already have two separate, fully specified Vega‑Lite line charts:

1. **Under‑5 mortality rate (per 1,000 live births), 2000–2023**  
   - [Under‑5 mortality trends in South Asia (2000–2023)](http://localhost:8000/static/viz_specs/13ebad9f-063d-4cae-bb63-66bd266d388a_vega.json)  
   - Indicator: *Mortality rate, under‑5 (per 1,000 live births)* — **SH.DYN.MORT** (`WB_WDI_SH_DYN_MORT`)

2. **Maternal mortality ratio (per 100,000 live births), 2000–2023**  
   - [Maternal mortality trends in South Asia (2000–2023)](http://localhost:8000/static/viz_specs/efac254d-117f-473a-b50d-ebaa9ddedb49_vega.json)  
   - Indicator: *Maternal mortality ratio (modeled estimate, per 100,000 live births)* — **SH.STA.MMRT** (`WB_WDI_SH_STA_MMRT`)

(There is also another under‑5 mortality spec at [this URL](http://localhost:8000/static/viz_specs/19d0c64c-f31c-4e49-aacf-5aac5883d76d_vega.json), but you can just use the first one.)

---

**Analysis / How to get a combined panel figure**

Because the visualization tool generates **one indicator per spec**, the combined panel has to be done in your own graphics or layout tool. Two straightforward options:

### Option A – Side‑by‑side or stacked panels in your article layout

1. **Export each chart as an image** (PNG/SVG) from your visualization environment.
2. In your layout tool (Word, Google Docs, InDesign, or your CMS):
   - Place **under‑5 mortality** on the **top** (or left).
   - Place **maternal mortality** on the **bottom** (or right).
3. Add panel titles and labels, for example:
   - Top panel title: “Under‑5 mortality rate, South Asia, 2000–2023 (per 1,000 live births)”
   - Bottom panel title: “Maternal mortality ratio, South Asia, 2000–2023 (per 100,000 live births)”
4. Use a **shared legend**:
   - Same country color set in both panels (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka).
   - Either:
     - Keep the legend in the **top panel only**, or  
     - Place a single legend between or below the panels and remove the duplicate.

This gives you exactly the two‑panel figure editors usually want, without editing the Vega specs.

### Option B – Combine Vega‑Lite specs manually (if you or your team use code)

If someone on your team is comfortable editing Vega‑Lite JSON:

1. Download the two specs from the URLs.
2. Wrap them in a single **Vega‑Lite vConcat or hConcat** spec, e.g. (sketch):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json",
  "vconcat": [
    { /* paste the under-5 mortality spec here, minus its $schema */ },
    { /* paste the maternal mortality spec here, minus its $schema */ }
  ]
}
```

3. Ensure:
   - Both use the same `color` encoding field (e.g. `REF_AREA`) and identical color scale so the legend is consistent.
   - Each panel has its own `title` that includes units:
     - “Under‑5 mortality rate (per 1,000 live births)”
     - “Maternal mortality ratio (per 100,000 live births)”
   - Optionally, move the `legend` definition to one panel and turn off the legend in the other with `"legend": null`.

This produces a single JSON spec you can embed as one combined chart.

---

**Note:**

- Axes will naturally be separate (different units and scales), which is what you want; trying to put both indicators on one y‑axis would be misleading.
- Keep **years (x‑axis)** aligned (2000–2023) for both panels; the generated specs already do this.

---

**Sources:**

- **World Bank — World Development Indicators (WDI)**  
  - SH.DYN.MORT — Mortality rate, under‑5 (per 1,000 live births)  
  - SH.STA.MMRT — Maternal mortality ratio (modeled estimate, per 100,000 live births)
